findings.claim: constraints.md states the v1 capture point two contradictory ways, 43 lines apart, with no marker on the wrong one. The Release Plan describes v1 as capture 'at source' / 'at creation' — the precise claim D-70 ratified as NOT the v1 claim, and which the same file forbids elsewhere. Both statements cannot hold: either v1 captures at source (requiring the DAW bridge 07.09 and a locally-installed client) or it captures at the first sharing moment (review link + session-close prompt). The file's own § Project Surfaces makes the former impossible by prohibiting every non-web client surface, so the Release Plan lines are residue from the pre-D-70 wording that the D-70 sweep missed. This matters beyond style because domain 07 D-06, quoted in problem-statement.md:39, makes it an obligation: 'the platform never overclaims what it cannot do — an overclaim discovered later is an unrecoverable trust breach', and v1 positioning copy is derived from these files.
findings.evidence: CONTRADICTING PAIR, both in meta/constraints.md. constraints.md:199 (§ v1 — the session spine): 'The irreducible wedge: hire → do the work → capture credit + split at source → on one identity.' and constraints.md:242 (§ Rights nuance): '**Rights nuance (unchanged)**: v1 includes split **capture** (cheap — a signed document at creation,'. CONTRADICTED BY, same file: constraints.md:205 (row 02 of the very same v1 table, 6 lines below line 199): 'the wedge — capture at the **first sharing moment** (D-70, 2026-07-22; capture-at-source is the *direction*, not the v1 claim — see § Project Surfaces, Desktop row)'; and constraints.md:292 (§ Project Surfaces, Desktop row): '**NOT AUTHORISED** (owner decision 2026-07-22, D-70). No WeJammin-installed client software runs on a user's own machine — no watch-folder agent, no DAW plugin, no other locally-installed binary. This is a rule, not an absence'. Corroborating the ratified wording, problem-statement.md:49-51: 'The honest v1 statement is therefore **"capture at the first sharing moment"**. That is still a structural advantage over reconstruction ... but it is not "present at the moment of creation", and nothing v1 ships may say that it is.' Neither line 199 nor line 242 carries any [PENDING]/[DEFERRED]/D-70 marker, and constraints.md has no open-questions section that would catch them.
findings.failure_scenario: A writer producing v1 launch copy, or a spec writer scoping the domain-09 split-capture slice, reads the § Release Plan — the section constraints.md itself calls 'the single most important input to /plan-phase' — and takes 'capture credit + split at source' literally. They either (a) ship marketing that claims capture at source, which D-06 classifies as an unrecoverable trust breach the first time a professional user checks, or (b) scope the v1 capture flow against a DAW/watch-folder trigger that § Project Surfaces prohibits outright, discovering only at /create-prd-stack that no client surface is authorised and the trigger must be rebuilt on the review link (07.05.02) and session-close prompt (07.06.02) instead.

findings.claim: The D-17 boundary verdict gives two different, irreconcilable counts for how many of the 101 boundary problems are resolved by mechanism extraction: the bolded verdict says ~85, the classification table immediately below says ~65. No reading reconciles them — the table assigns 'Extract Section-1 mechanism' to exactly one class (~65); the other three classes are resolved as 'None — leave as-is' (~10 clean seams), 'Suppress spurious rows in assembler' (2 tooling mis-tags) and 'See below' (~8 merge candidates). The four classes also sum to ~85 against a stated pool of 101, leaving ~16 boundary problems with no class and no resolution. Neither statement carries a marker, so a reader cannot tell which is authoritative or whether 16 problems were dropped.
findings.evidence: cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md:239 (§ 3 Verdict, bolded): '**The fix for ~85 of the 101 is mechanism extraction per Section 1 — not domain merger.**' CONTRADICTED BY cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md:252 (§ Classification summary table, the only row whose Resolution column is mechanism extraction): '| Unowned coordination seams / cross-cut mis-modelled as feature | ~65 | B3, B20, B22, B31, B39, B46, B52, B64, B76, B85, B91, B94 | **Extract Section-1 mechanism** |'. The other three rows, cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md:250-253, resolve differently: '| Clean / defended seams (evidence FOR split) | ~10 | ... | None — leave as-is |', '| Tooling mis-tags (not real seams) | 2 | ... | Suppress spurious rows in assembler |', '| Genuine merge / shared-owner candidates | ~8 | ... | See below |'. Pool size is fixed at cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md:5: 'Source pool: 83 candidate emergent cross-cuts (`emCC`), 90 candidate emergent features (`emF`), 101 boundary problems (`bp`).' 10 + 2 + 65 + 8 = 85, not 101.
findings.failure_scenario: /create-prd inherits this file as its boundary-work backlog (declared at line 7-10: 'Downstream contract: /create-prd (architecture + shared-mechanism registry), /decompose-architecture ... inherit this file'). The architect sizes the mechanism-extraction workstream from the bolded verdict at ~85 items, then reconciles against the table and finds only ~65 classified as extraction work — a 20-item discrepancy with no list to resolve it — and separately cannot account for the ~16 boundary problems (101 minus 85) that appear in no class at all, so cannot tell whether they were judged benign or simply never triaged.

findings.claim: The Purchased-Input Clearance Propagation cross-cut raises a load-bearing design fork inline — push-at-purchase versus pull-as-of-at-release — with no owner, no deferral target, and no tracking anywhere in the ideation tree. The file has no Open Questions section at all (its only headings are § 1, § 2, § 3 and Related Specs), so the question has nowhere to live. This is not a case of tracked deferral: I searched the whole tree for both 'push-at-purchase' and 'Purchased-Input Clearance' and neither string occurs in any file other than this one. Contrast the neighbouring '(tentative)' mechanism two rows above, which IS properly tracked — ideation-cx.md § 1b 'Candidate Mechanisms (unratified)' carries Practice-Room Tools with both a 'Deciding question' and a 'Target stage' column — which demonstrates the tracking mechanism exists in this tree and was simply not applied here.
findings.evidence: cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md:124 (§ 1h, full row): '| **Purchased-Input Clearance Propagation** | A paid purchase becomes dated, machine-readable clearance **evidence** that travels downstream (placement → project 07 → release 12 → rights 09), carrying the *right* not the *use*. Related to but distinct from Verified-Credit-as-Evidence (trigger is a purchase, not a countersigned credit). Open Q: push-at-purchase vs pull-as-of-at-release. | 07,09,12,14 |'. The trailing 'Open Q:' has no owner column, no target stage, and no question identifier. File headings (confirmed by grep '^#'): line 1 title, line 20 '## 1. New Cross-Cut Mechanisms', line 129 '## 2. New Features by Domain', line 223 '## 3. Boundary Analysis & D-17 Verdict', line 276 '## Related Specs' — there is no '## Open Questions' section. Tree-wide search over 1,121 ideation .md files (via find|xargs, after confirming recursive grep was broken) returns 0 files containing 'push-at-purchase' and 0 containing 'Purchased-Input Clearance' outside this file. Compare the correctly-tracked sibling at cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md:123 whose question is carried in ideation-cx.md:50 with an explicit Target stage column.
findings.failure_scenario: Two implementers building clearance propagation for the same v1.5/phase-2 surface resolve the fork opposite ways and both are defensible from this text. One pushes a clearance record downstream at purchase time, so a sample bought today is permanently marked cleared on the project even if the vendor's own upstream licence is later found invalid; the other pulls as-of at release, so the release-time check re-evaluates and can block a release the first implementer would have shipped. The two produce different stored data, different failure modes at release gate 12, and different answers to 'was this track cleared?' — and because the question is registered nowhere, no stage is scheduled to decide it before code is written.

findings.claim: Two files in this unit self-declare completion status `[DEEP]` while the pipeline key file records both as `[PARTIAL]`. The status vocabulary is a gating signal that downstream workflows read to decide whether a document is safe to consume, so a document cannot be both. Neither side carries a reconciling note, and the index rows are not marked as deliberate downgrades. Note the index is internally selective about this — it records `[DEEP]` for the other four meta documents, matching their headers exactly — so the two mismatches read as drift rather than a convention that index status means something different from file status.
findings.evidence: SELF-DECLARED: constraints.md:3 — '> Status: `[DEEP]` — all constraint categories resolved during `/ideate-validate` 2026-07-18.' and competitive-landscape.md:3 — '> Status: `[DEEP]` — completed `/ideate-validate` 2026-07-18.' CONTRADICTED BY the pipeline key file ideation-index.md § Meta Documents: line 94 — '| Competitive Landscape | [competitive-landscape.md](meta/competitive-landscape.md) | `[PARTIAL]` |' and line 95 — '| Constraints | [constraints.md](meta/constraints.md) | `[PARTIAL]` |'. The same index table agrees with the file header for every other meta document: line 91 Problem Statement `[DEEP]`, line 92 Personas `[DEEP]` (4 primary), line 93 Counterparty Profiles `[DEEP]`, line 96 Cross-Cut Emergent Capabilities `[DEEP]` (Step 6). Both file headers additionally assert positive completion language ('all constraint categories resolved', 'completed /ideate-validate') that is incompatible with PARTIAL.
findings.failure_scenario: CLAUDE.md establishes that ideation-index.md is the pipeline key file all downstream workflows read first. /create-prd reads the index, sees Constraints `[PARTIAL]`, and re-opens the constraint interview — re-asking the owner for budget, timeline, team and compliance values that constraints.md:3 states were already resolved and locked on 2026-07-18, including the 'Locked Technical Constraints (user-declared)' the file explicitly says are 'inputs to /create-prd, not open decisions for it'. Conversely an agent trusting the file header treats the competitive landscape as closed and skips the Q-04 positioning re-read the index's PARTIAL was plausibly flagging.

findings.claim: The emergent-capability inventory counts recorded against this file in the index and in ratified decision D-27 do not match the file's actual contents: D-27 records 52 mechanisms and 76 features; the file contains 54 mechanism rows and 83 feature rows. That is 2 mechanisms and 7 features present in the authoritative table but absent from the ratified count, with nothing marking which they are or when they were added. Because the file declares its § 1 table to be 'the authoritative extract-me-as-shared list' that downstream stages inherit, the gap means a reviewer reconciling the deliverable against the ratified decision cannot tell whether the extra 9 entries are legitimate later additions or unratified content.
findings.evidence: ACTUAL CONTENT, counted programmatically over meta/cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md (markdown data rows, excluding header and separator rows, § 1a-1h and § 2 respectively): 54 mechanism rows and 83 feature rows. RECORDED COUNTS, ideation-index.md:78 — '| Emergent cross-cuts / features (Step 6) | 52 / 76 — [meta/cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md](meta/cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md) |' and ideation-index.md:213 (decision D-27) — '**Emergent capabilities persisted** to [meta/cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md](meta/cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md): **52 new cross-cut mechanisms** and **76 new features** surfaced during synthesis'. The file's own header states only the pre-dedup candidate pool, cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md:4-5: 'Source pool: 83 candidate emergent cross-cuts (`emCC`), 90 candidate emergent features (`emF`), 101 boundary problems (`bp`)' — so 52/76 cannot be read as the candidate figures, and the file itself states no post-dedup total. Authority of the table is asserted at cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md:8-9: 'The **New Cross-Cut Mechanisms** table is the authoritative "extract-me-as-shared" list — anything here must NOT be rebuilt per-domain.'
findings.failure_scenario: /create-prd commissions the shared-mechanism registry from D-27's ratified figure of 52 mechanisms, builds 52, and reconciles clean against the decision record while 2 mechanisms in the authoritative table are never extracted — and because no entry is flagged as post-D-27, the two silently fall through to being rebuilt per-domain, which is the exact outcome line 9 exists to prevent. The same gap on the feature side leaves 7 of the 83 enumerated feature deficits outside any ratified count.
